text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Relaunch of Fokker scrapped as receivers cease negotiations with South Korean company Samsung. (p1)
- Dutch/Belgian financial services group Fortis first nine months net jumps 18 pct; company adjusts full year earnings forecast upwards. (p1)
- KNP BT Packaging speeds up plans for takeovers. (p3)
- Rabobank suffers no loss from Fokker bankruptcy. (p3)
- Trading company Internatio-Mueller takes over Germany's distributor of chemicals Chemie Beteiligungsgesellschaft. (CBG). (p4)
- Philips Electronics to restructure production of televisions; Italian plant closes next year, job loss in Belgium and France. (p4)
- Publisher Elsevier merges two of its magazine publishing units, Bonaventura and Misset. (p4)
- Dutch GDP growth accelerates. (p5)
VOLKSKRANT
- Interior minister Hans Dijkstal hopeful of a quick agreement on European drugs policy. (p1)
- Medium-sized firms expect strong job growth in 1997. (p2)
- Finance minister Gerrit Zalm to talk with banks about passing on costs of Euro conversion to customers. (p3)
- European commission threatens to fine shipping cartel TACA in which Nedlloyd participates. (p17)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Dutch public is sick of being polled by marketing agencies. (p3)
- Food and detergent concern Unilever sells its ice-cream unit Hertog to the Brinkers group. (p29)
- Strong interest in bourse launch of bedroom furniture group Beter Bed: subscription to close today. (p29)
- Dutch stock market guru Rienk Kamer forecasts recession for Western industrialised countries until 2000. (p 31)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Industrial concern Stork does not suffer from cancellation ot takeover talks with Samsung. (p13)
- Shipping and tank storage concern Van Ommeren takes over tank storage companies in Brazil and Chile. (p13)
TROUW
- Growing number of MPs want state to put money in Fokker's participation in Airbus project. (p1)
